title: 2-Year Floating Rate Note auction (quarterly new issue) — sells on the FOMC decision day
source: EST: treasury.gov Tentative Schedule of Treasury Auctions PDF, text layer decompressed direct 2026-09-05 (plain curl, HTTP 200, 17,195 bytes) — row reads `2-Year FRN / Announcement Thursday, October 22, 2026 / Auction Wednesday, October 28, 2026 / Settlement Monday, November 02, 2026`, and carries NO `R` marker while the 08-20, 09-17, 11-19 and 12-17 FRN rows in the same PDF all read `2-Year FRNR` — i.e. this is the quarterly new issue. Size corroborated in advance by press release sb0590 (2026-08-05), read as text direct 2026-09-05, whose Oct-26 anticipated-size row reads 30 in the FRN column (header `2-Year 3-Year 5-Year 7-Year 10-Year 20-Year 30-Year FRN`, row `69 58 70 44 39 13 22 30`); the auction record agrees independently, with 10 consecutive quarterly new issues at $30B since 2024-04-24 and 20 consecutive reopenings at $28B since 2024-05-29 (fiscaldata auctions_query, floating_rate:Yes, pulled 2026-09-05). Stays estimate on two counts: a tentative schedule is tentative by construction, and this lane may not self-confirm an event it discovered in-sweep — the confirming primary is the 2026-10-22 announcement itself. The ~11:30 ET auction slot is NOT sourced and is deliberately omitted
notes: The one security of the four sized by treasury-coupon-announcement-2026-10-22 that had no calendar row, while treasury-2y-note-2026-10-26, treasury-5y-note-2026-10-27 and treasury-7y-note-2026-10-29 all did — and the only one selling on an FOMC decision day (fomc-2026-10-28). That pairing LOOKS like supply into a policy event and is measured NOT to be: crossing all 69 FRN auctions from 2021-01-01 to 2026-09-04 against the Fed's own published decision dates, 9 sold on a decision day and 8 of the 9 were quarterly new issues (2021-01-27, 2021-07-28, 2022-01-26, 2022-07-27, 2023-07-26, 2025-10-29, 2026-01-28, 2026-07-29) — 8 of 23 new issues, ~35%, because Treasury's FRN new-issue slot sits in the last week of January/April/July/October and the FOMC's meetings end in that same week. The raw margin gap (high discount margin 7.05bp on-FOMC vs 13.17bp off) is composition, not effect; within-CUSIP controls remove the level and show nothing — DM(first reopening) minus DM(its own new issue) is +0.43bp on-FOMC vs +0.70bp off, and DM(new issue) minus DM(the immediately preceding auction) is -1.23bp on vs -0.70bp off. Mechanism claimed: an FRN indexed to the 13-week bill resets weekly and absorbs the decision. Live context: the discount margin is at a FOUR-YEAR LOW — 5.0bp on 2026-07-29 and 5.5bp on 2026-08-26, the last sub-5.0bp print being 2022-07-27 — with a named but unmeasured mechanism, sb0590's own 'SOMA purchases of Treasury bills and growing demand for Treasury bills from the private sector'. The one FRN auction between now and this one is the 2026-09-23 reopening, which is the free read on whether that low is a level or a moment. Read-it-do-not-trade-it: `symbols: []`, the date is `estimate`, and no house playbook (S1/S2/E1/S3/S4 + G1) is rates-keyed. This event does NOT re-register the prediction: FT-treasury-coupon-announcement-2026-10-22-2 already owns the discount-margin test and scores 2026-10-29 — inherit it rather than duplicating one observation. Discovered during the treasury-coupon-announcement-2026-10-22 initial research (2026-09-05), which found this calendar had never recorded a floating-rate note or a discount margin at all.
